entries.proposition: THE DUPLICATION AS PRINTED: array CGH, hg18 coordinates, size 0.744-0.827 Mb, inheritance unknown.

THE AUTHORS' DOSE INTERPRETATION, which this reading tests against the coordinates: mapped to GRCh37 the interval covers only the last WWOX exon and the 3' part of intron 8 (plus MAF), not the whole gene.
entries.snippet: The duplication found in Patient 1 affects two dose-sensitive genes: WWOX (OMIM 605131) and MAF (OMIM 177075).

entries.proposition: SEGREGATION NOT ESTABLISHED: no paternal DNA; the significance is called limited by the authors.
entries.snippet: The significance of this change in our patient is limited by the lack of paternal DNA and detailed clinical data about speech development in the father.

entries.proposition: PHENOTYPE BAND: a non-progressive neurodevelopmental disorder with severe expressive language impairment and declining nonverbal IQ, plus epilepsy whose EEG normalised on valproate. Not a DEE band.
entries.snippet: epilepsy—valproic acid resulted in a complete EEG normalization

entries.proposition: PHENOTYPE BAND, cognitive course: nonverbal IQ falling across repeated testing.
entries.snippet: 6 yr—nonverbal Leiter scale IQ-75; 11 yr and 13 yr—nonverbal scale of the WISC-R test IQ 52; 17 yr—nonverbal scale of the WISC-R test IQ 42

entries.proposition: THE LINK TO WWOX IS SPECULATIVE in the authors' own words.
entries.snippet: It is difficult to attribute deep speech and language impairment, which dominates in the clinical picture of this patient, to the duplication of a specific gene
